carnage.name: patman
carnage.commentary: Hole 12 turned into a full-on leak: 7 gross, 5 net, and not a single shot-level bailout in the feed. That’s what 39 putts and six 3-putts smell like anyway.

carnage.name: Factor_Golf
carnage.commentary: Hole 10 was the crime scene: 7 gross, 5 net, zero shot detail, all damage. Hard to look at 17.07 strokes lost and pretend this thing was anything but a total wipeout.

carnage.name: RosaryJoe
carnage.commentary: Hole 18 slapped him with a 5 gross, 5 net finish and left the card looking pretty damn ordinary. The round was otherwise fine, but that closing bogey-sized bruise gave the hole-to-hole story a gross ending.

carnage.name: czxzt
carnage.commentary: Hole 9 was the lone blemish: 4 gross, 4 net, nothing flashy in the shot log, just a one-over slip. Otherwise this was the kind of card that hides the missed chances behind a clean number.

carnage.name: llyreks
carnage.commentary: Hole 4 is where the card coughed up its first bad taste: 4 gross, 4 net, no shot sequence to polish it up. Not a disaster, just the sort of wobble that keeps a good round from becoming a stupidly low one.

carnage.name: GimmeG
carnage.commentary: Hole 10 was a rare hiccup: 4 gross, 2 net, and the feed gives no shot-by-shot rescue story. When you’re still winning net by 18 and your worst hole is barely a hiccup, the rest of the field can eat the dust.

players.name: GimmeG
players.tagline: Even the “bad” holes barely qualified as a cough.
players.body: GimmeG ran away with the net title at 33 under and still only had to swallow one of those tiny par-3 paper cuts on the worst hole. The raw card was obviously not perfect — 15th gross at plus 1 — but the sim was basically handing out free candy: 4.99 strokes gained approach, 1.96 short game, and a ridiculous 6.95 tee to green. The stat line backs it up too: 10 GIR, 28 putts, just two 3-putts, and 79 feet of putts made. The only real blemish was hole 10, where a 4 gross and 2 net kept the disaster in the “lol whatever” category. After one prior start that finished 15th net and 28th gross, this is a massive leap and not some cute little improvement; it’s the dude actually showing up and nuking the field.

players.name: patman
players.tagline: A net podium built on vibes and a full-blown putting dumpster fire.
players.body: patman somehow grabbed second net at minus 15 while posting a gross finish of 44th and looking like the course had personally insulted him. The scorecard was brutal: 39 putts, six 3-putts, nine bogeys, three doubles-plus, and only one birdie. That’s not a round, that’s a slow-motion yard sale. The SG numbers explain the whole mess: minus 1.86 approach, minus 4.19 short game, and a grossly ugly minus 7.03 putting for minus 13.07 total. Hole 12 was the ugliest swing, with a 7 gross and 5 net, and hole 10 wasn’t much prettier at 6 gross. The weird part is the net result is still strong enough to cash in second, which says more about the field than the swing path. After a prior start that was 35th net and 44th gross, this is a huge net jump, but it came with enough raw carnage to make your eyes bleed.

players.name: Factor_Golf
players.tagline: A five-birdie round would be nice. This was the opposite of that.
players.body: Factor_Golf took third net at minus 11, but the gross card was a flaming mess at 46th and plus 25. The strangest part is how empty the birdie column stayed: zero birdies, five bogeys, five doubles-plus, and 32 putts that did absolutely nothing to stop the bleeding. The strokes gained story is ugly across the board: minus 5.32 approach, minus 7.77 short game, minus 3.98 putting, and minus 17.07 total. Hole 10 was the ugliest hit with a 7 gross and 5 net, and there were also 6s on holes 3 and 9, which is a hell of a way to spend a par-3 day. Compared with the prior start, where the player was 41st net and 45th gross, the net side moved up, but only because the rest of the field left the door open while this card stayed stuck in the mud.

players.name: czxzt
players.tagline: Clean card, clean steal, and the best kind of annoying.
players.body: czxzt came in with no prior profile baggage and immediately dropped a fourth-place net finish at minus 2, while matching that with fourth gross at minus 2. That’s the cleanest little pair of numbers in this batch and the SG backs it up hard: plus 6.87 approach, plus 0.84 short game, plus 2.22 putting, and plus 9.93 total. The card was balanced enough to survive one bad-ish hole, with 13 greens in regulation, zero 3-putts, only two bogeys, and 119 feet of putts made. Hole 9 was the worst spot on the sheet, a 4 gross and 4 net, but that’s basically a paper cut on a round that was otherwise doing work. Four birdies on a par-3/executive setup is the kind of thing that keeps the rest of the room pissed off and looking at their own cards like they owe them money.

players.name: RosaryJoe
players.tagline: Held it together just long enough to keep the round from getting stupid.
players.body: RosaryJoe finished fifth net at even par and 17th gross at plus 3, which is a pretty clean summary of a round that had some good pieces without ever really detonating. The stats are solid, not sexy: 8 GIR, 26 putts, one 3-putt, one birdie, and a pair of bogeys with only one double-plus showing up. Short game was the best part at plus 2.97 SG, with approach at plus 1.85 and tee to green at plus 4.82, so the ball-striking and scrambling did enough to keep the card in shape. Hole 18 was the worst hole, a 5 gross and 5 net, which is a pretty annoying way to end when the rest of the round was mostly respectable. This is better net than the prior 12th-place finish, and the short-game profile still looks like the thing keeping him afloat, but the scoring ceiling is still getting capped by too many holes that just sit there and refuse to turn into birdies.

players.name: llyreks
players.tagline: The ball-striking showed up; the putter mostly filed a complaint.
players.body: llyreks posted sixth net at plus 1 and seventh gross at minus 1, which is a rare case where the raw and net numbers both say the round was pretty damn competent. The SG split is the story: plus 8.84 approach, plus 1.64 short game, minus 1.56 putting, and plus 8.93 total. That’s a ball-striking day with just enough missed looks to keep it from being truly filthy. He had 12 GIR, only three bogeys, and no doubles-plus, but the 29 putts and two 3-putts kept the ceiling from getting stupid low. Hole 4 was the worst hole at 4 gross and 4 net, and holes 5 and 11 also blinked with 4s, which is the kind of “mostly fine” golf that still leaves a few shots sitting on the table. Compared with the prior start, this is another solid run and a little better net finish, but the profile still says the putter is the guy in the group refusing to chip in for gas.
